Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a draft runbook and our current network boundary diagram for the private deployment pattern we reviewed. High level answers up front:

- HSM placement: customer VPC private subnet, dedicated hardware HSM (SecureKey-by-default for this pilot) accessed only via an internal management subnet with restricted SGs; all HSM control plane and admin ports are source-restricted to our operator bastions and the customer's site-to-site VPN endpoints.
- BYOK lifecycle: operator creates a CEK locally, wraps it with the HSM KEK (non-exportable), stores wrapped CEK in our encrypted metadata store (redwood-kv). Rotation is automated via a rotation job; emergency rollover uses a secondary KEK (pre-provisioned) and a short canary rollout.
- Impact to in-flight requests: for rolling rotations we maintain old KEK for unwrap-latency window; requests continue to be served while we rewrap CEKs in the background — brief latency spike possible during rewrap at scale.

Attachments: redwood_byo_rotation_draft_v1.pdf, hsm-network-boundary-20270612.png

Next steps: Karthik / Mina, can you review the operator steps in the draft and call out any gaps for Atlas? Also tagging Soojin for the audit/a11y of logs.

Best,
Alex

Maya / Alex — quick technical supplements after reviewing the draft: 

1) Network boundary specifics (for the diagram):
   - Management plane: HSM management interface limited to 10.0.5.0/28 (operator bastions) and the customer VPN endpoint 198.51.100.32/32. ACL: deny all ingress other than IPs above; restrict ports to 22 (bastion only), 7900-7920 for vendor management channel (per SecureKey spec).
   - Data plane: all model inference traffic never touches HSM; only the key-wrap/unwrap RPCs go to HSM over an internal mTLS channel on port 8444. HSM sits in an isolated subnet with no Internet egress.

2) Key material controls and rotation:
   - KEK non-exportability: vendor HSM enforces non-export of the KEK; Redwood maintains wrapped CEKs only.
   - Rotation cadence and window: template: quarterly scheduled rotation + emergency rotation procedure. Rotation job creates new KEK in HSM, rewraps active CEKs in a staged manner (canaries by tenant shard), verifies successful unwrap, then retires old KEK after 72h verification window.
   - Operator procedures: preflight checks (backup of encrypted metadata only), notify active tenants, pause cross-region sync during rollover, monitor rewrap success matrix.

3) Audit & access:
   - All HSM admin ops produce signed audit events forwarded to customer SIEM over an encrypted forwarder; we retain audit artifacts per contract (90/365 days per account tier).

4) Failure modes and mitigations:
   - HSM hardware failure: failover to warm-redundant HSM in same AZ with rewrapped CEKs; if cross-AZ failover needed we instantiate a read-only failover and route control-plane through the bastion.
   - Unwrap failures: automatic rollback to previous KEK; alert, and pause rotation.

I'll add these bullets into the runbook. Also noting SecureKey has a provider attestation PDF — pinged them below to include the cert chain and FIPS statement.

-Karthik

Attaching SecureKey integration notes and our FIPS/CC attestation (see securekey-integration-notes-20270614.pdf). A few clarifications that will help Atlas for the compliance review: 

- FIPS mode: SecureKey HSMs can be run in FIPS 140-2 Level 2 mode; the attestation PDF includes cert numbers and the vendor CA chain.
- Operator roles: vendor supports remote HSM patching but requires a vendor-maintained support account which we can scope to read-only for operator operations; recommend use of just-in-time vendor access via ephemeral tokens.
- Key wrap/unwrap: we only permit wrap/unwrap via mTLS client certs; we provide a CA bundle for Redwood to pin.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the attestation items if that helps your auditors.
